Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks from our procurement/CFO team: we like the overall approach of keeping the inference runtime in our VPC but need clarity on (1) how the platform fee is amortized for pilots vs. long-term, (2) the available SLA tiers and response windows if we need an on-call escalation, and (3) a simpler one-page price summary for our finance team.

Two constraints to flag up-front: our budget owner wants any non-recurring platform fee capped in year 1 to $200k, and the CFO prefers subscription amortization over a large upfront perpetual license.

Can you send options (A/B/C) that map to pilot -> full production transitions? Also please include typical migration support hours and any onboarding credit for the pilot.

Best,
Alan

--

Subject: Re: Northstar Health - phased platform fee & SLA options for VPC/on-prem deployment

Alan — thanks for the clear asks. I put together three concrete commercial options and attached a one-page summary and the detailed pricing model (see attachments). High level:

Option A - Pilot-first, subscription amortized
- 6-month pilot: platform fee waived for first 3 months, then 50% platform fee for months 4-6 (credit applied)
- Production start (month 7): standard annual platform subscription amortized monthly
- Support: Bronze (standard) included during pilot; can buy Silver/Gold as add-on
- Estimated year-1 cost (pilot + 6 months prod): $180k - meets your $200k cap for year 1 in our example load profile.

Option B - Small upfront platform fee with onboarding credit
- One-time platform initiation fee (amortized by us as credit over first year) capped at $120k
- Ongoing platform subscription lower than A (5% discount in year 2 if commit to 24 months)
- Onboarding: 40 hours migration support included, additional hours at discounted rate

Option C - Perpetual license + optional support tiers (not your preference but offered for completeness)
- Perpetual license price quoted; separate annual support (tiered)
- For finance: we provide capitalization language and sample journal entries.

SLA/support tiers (summary)
- Bronze (included): business hours support, 24-hour response for Sev1
- Silver (recommended for production): 24/7 monitoring, 4-hour response for Sev1, 8x5 priority engineering hours per month
- Gold (enterprise): 24/7 1-hour response for Sev1, 24/7 on-call rotation, runbook consulting, up to 40 engineering hours/month

We think Option A maps best to your preference to avoid a large upfront capital outlay while preserving flexibility. We also included a pilot credit to keep year-1 spend inside your $200k cap in the attached workbook.

Attached: NSH_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft), pricing_model_staggered.xlsx, redwood-enterprise-terms-2027.docx

Would it help if I put Vivek and Stephanie on a 30-minute call with your procurement + finance to walk the one-pager and the workbook?

Thanks,
Tessa

--

Alan — quick follow-up from the product/finance side. Two practical notes to help procurement: 1) amortization approach — we can offer a 12-month subscription invoice schedule for the platform fee so your accounting treats it as operating expense, and 2) pilot credits are formalized as invoice credits (not refunds) and can be applied to the year-1 subscription.

On SLAs: our Gold tier requires a minimum commitment (either a capacity commit or 24-month term) because the on-call rotation is staffed. If you want Gold without a term, we can present an hourly retainer alternative.

Suggested minimal commercial language for your CFO: "Platform subscription will be invoiced monthly over a 12-month term; startup credits will be applied as invoice credits during the first 12 months. Annual support fees are invoiced yearly and are eligible for amortization per company accounting practices." We can add that to the SOW.

Happy to join a call next week to walk the CFO through the invoice examples.

Vivek

Tessa/Vivek — thanks for the clear options and the language for the CFO; that helps a lot. A couple quick decisions from our side:

- We prefer Option A (Pilot-first) with the 3-month waiver and 50% months 4-6 as you outlined.
- For year-1 budgeting we want the subscription amortized monthly per Vivek's suggestion.
- Support: we want to commit to Silver for production and would consider Gold if we sign a 24-month capacity commit.

Next steps: Grace (CFO) wants the one-page summary and the SOW with the amortization clause added and the platform fee cap language (year-1 cap $200k). Can your legal/SOW team send an updated SOW and a single-page commercial summary by EOD Friday (Feb 12)? Also please include the DocuSign link for signatures.

Appreciate it — Alan
